paper.title_en: A catalogue of insights from the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
paper.abstract_en: Over the last decade, gravitational-wave science has developed from a detection being a Nobel-winning achievement to an (almost) everyday occurrence. The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) Collaboration's flagship scientific results are now their catalogues of detections. We review discoveries from the fourth observing run (O4) of the \ac{LVK}. The recent catalogues each include $\sim100$ new detections. Among these are remarkable single discoveries: the loudest signals detected, and sources unlike those seen before. However, significant advances also are coming from population-level analyses, leveraging the sample size to infer constraints on the astrophysical distribution of merging compact binaries, potential deviations from general relativity, and the expansion rate of the Universe. Analyses of the latest data have revealed evidence for multiple subpopulations of sources, providing a unique probe into the evolution of coalescing binaries. Our understanding of gravitational-wave signals and their sources will continue to deepen with more observations: the final catalogue from O4 will release in December 2026, and planned future observing runs with greater detector sensitivity will bring even larger catalogues and additional loud signals.
